title: ci.yml: add permissions: contents: read (rust jobs run with default GITHUB_TOKEN)
description: Security review finding (mbzu pass-2): ci.yml has no permissions block, so all jobs run with the repo-default GITHUB_TOKEN; rust-build-test/clippy/all-features compile cloned external content (oscore-fork build.rs executes). Workflow never writes via the token. Fix: permissions: contents: read at workflow top level (or per-job) in ci.yml; check other workflows too.
close_reason: Fixed: added top-level 'permissions: contents: read' to all 7 workflows that lacked it (ci, coverity, ec2-arm64, fuzz, mutation, renode-firmware, renode), matching interop.yml's existing pattern. Checked every workflow first: no GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN/gh-CLI writes anywhere, no OIDC id-token consumers (renode-firmware uses static AWS keys), caches/artifacts use the runtime token (unaffected). All 8 YAML files parse. 3x delegated codereview (kimi-k3): all PASS. Two pre-existing observations filed separately: tvw5 (fork-PR self-hosted runner gate) and bttv (renode-firmware failure-bead never persisted).
